newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FOCUS - Irish Ryanair shares soar on market debut.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Irish Ryanair shares soar on market debut.

text.p: Shares in Irish low-cost airline Ryanair Holdings Plc soared on Ireland's stock exchange on Thursday after their launch was more than 18 times oversubscribed, dealers said.
Ryanair said it was delighted with the response to its share offer. The shares were initially priced at 195 Irish pence, at the top end of expectations, and immediately started heading higher.

Although official trading in the shares does not begin on Ireland's stock exchange until June 5, unofficial "grey market" dealing dominated the Irish market. The shares leaped to 261p within 10 minutes of their grey market launch and were "heading for three pounds a share", dealers said.
Ryanair's American Depositary shares RYAAY.O, which will represent five ordinary shares, were priced at $14.73.
Ryanair's floatation on both New York's Nasdaq and Ireland's ISEQ index is the first time an Irish company has sought a simultaneous quote in both Ireland and the U.S.

"We are delighted with the response to the IPO (initial public offering) on both sides of the Atlantic," Ryanair said in a statement after the launch. "The flotation is a significant step in establishing Ryanair as Europe's leading low-fares airline."

Ryanair said there was a 50-50 split in take-up of stock between the United States and Europe, and 86 percent of Ryanair employees had subscribed for a total of 2.2 million Irish pounds ($3.3 million) worth of shares.
The flotation price capitalises the airline at 308 million Irish pounds.

Ryanair, which has been operating for 12 years and has a fleet of 13 Boeing 737-200 aircraft, with a future delivery of six new aircraft expected by November, said the funds raised will be used to cut debt, which is now 35 million Irish pounds.
It will also allow the airline to be in a position to buy aircraft when necessary, Ryanair said when it announced its intention to float on May 6.
Speculation the company would seek a listing mounted after U.S. entrepreneur David Bonderman became Ryanair chairman in December 1996 after taking a 20 percent stake in the airline.

Bonderman took over from former GPA chief Tony Ryan whose family founded Ryanair. After the offer, the Ryan family will own 35.3 percent of the company, down from 61.7 percent, while Irish Air and chief executive Michael O'Leary will own 15.7 and 14.1 percent respectively.
Ryanair said in its statement on May 6 that its strategy was to aim for 20 to 30 percent sales growth a year and increase flights on existing routes.
Morgan Stanley & Co International Ltd were appointed global co-ordinator and bookrunner for the issue.

The offer was underwritten by Morgan Stanley, Investment Bank of Ireland, CS First Boston and the Robinson Humphrey Company, Inc. Morgan Stanley and IBI Corporate Finance acted as joint sponsors and financial advisers to Ryanair and Davy Stockbrokers were brokers to the issue. ($ = 0.662 Irish Pounds)
